content: Decomposing a single-file app into multi-file native ES modules without a build step has two hard blockers over python -m http.server: (1) ES modules require a JavaScript MIME type and Python 3.12 serves .jsx/.tsx as application/octet-stream (verified locally: mimetypes.guess_type('x.jsx') = (None,None)), so <script type=module src=app.jsx> fails; (2) the only browser-side JSX compilers for external files are Babel standalone (XHR-based, MIME-agnostic) and none of the esm.sh loaders (run has no src support, verified). The viable pattern is multiple external <script type='text/babel' src='js/*.jsx'> tags: Babel loads them via XHR, executes in document order, all classic scripts share the global lexical scope so cross-file references work. Files must not use import/export. Serving over HTTP is required (XHR fails under file://).
